slides.title: The nurse is performing an assessment on an older adult client. Which manifestations are considered normal age-related changes in the eye? Select all that apply.
text: The nurse is performing an assessment on an older adult client. Which manifestations are considered normal age-related changes in the eye? Select all that apply.
Increased ability to discriminate among colors.

slides.title: Clear lens.  No, the lens becomes cloudy.
text: Clear lens.  No, the lens becomes cloudy.
Blurred vision. Yes, vision becomes blurry with age progression.
Protruding cornea. No, this is not a normal age-related change.
Increased tear production. No, they have a decreased tear production.
Diminished pupillary adaptation to darkness. Yes, this is a normal age-related change.
Increased ability to discriminate among colors. No, they have a decreased ability to discriminate among colors.

slides.title: Normal Aging Process
text: Information processing decreases but cognitive ability does not

slides.title: Normal Aging Process
text: Diminished blood flow to the lungs
Takes longer to recover from stress or shock
Rigid rib cage with decreased expansion

slides.title: Educating Clients
text: Establish who is involved with the care

slides.title: Health Promotion and Maintenance
text: Primary Prevention – health promotion and health protection (ex. teaching about lifestyle)
Secondary Prevention – screening, early diagnosis and treatment (ex. mammogram)
Tertiary Prevention – rehabilitation and palliative care (ex. foot care for a diabetic)

slides.title: The nurse is working at an osteoporosis screening clinic. Which of the following female clients is at greatest risk for developing osteoporosis? Select all that apply.
text: The nurse is working at an osteoporosis screening clinic. Which of the following female clients is at greatest risk for developing osteoporosis? Select all that apply.
A female who started menopause early.
A female with a family history of osteoporosis.
A female who has a physically active lifestyle.
A female with an inadequate intake of calcium and vitamin D.

slides.title: An Asian female. Yes, Asian and Caucasian females are prone to osteoporosis.
text: An Asian female. Yes, Asian and Caucasian females are prone to osteoporosis.
A large frame, dark skinned female. No, its common in small framed females.
A female who started menopause early. Yes, menopause predisposes females to osteoporosis.
A female with a family history of the disease. Yes, genetics predisposes females to osteoporosis.
A female who has a physically active lifestyle. No, those with a sedentary lifestyle are prone to osteoporosis.
A female with an inadequate intake of calcium and vitamin D. Yes, calcium and vitamin D deficiency are associated with osteoporosis.

slides.title: The charge nurse is re-assigning client rooms to accommodate new admissions. Which of the following clients should the nurse assign to the same room? Select all that apply.
text: The charge nurse is re-assigning client rooms to accommodate new admissions. Which of the following clients should the nurse assign to the same room? Select all that apply.
32-year-old female that is  2-day post op cholecystectomy and a 40-year-old female with pain due to pancreatitis.
36-year-old female with diarrhea/vomiting of unknown origin and a 31-year-old female receiving chemotherapy for colon cancer.
82-year-old male with pneumonia/candidiasis of the groin and a 76-year-old male with upper respiratory infection/thrush.
46-year-old male with MRSA infection and a 50-year-old male with C.difficile  infection.
18-year-old female that is 1-day post op appendectomy and an 84-year-old female who is agitated and confused.

slides.title: 32-year-old female that is  2-day post op cholecystectomy and a 40-year-old female with pain due to pancreatitis. Yes, similar age, both post-op and nothing contagious.
text: 32-year-old female that is  2-day post op cholecystectomy and a 40-year-old female with pain due to pancreatitis. Yes, similar age, both post-op and nothing contagious.

36-year-old female with diarrhea/vomiting of unknown origin and a 31-year-old female receiving chemotherapy for colon cancer. No, one client is immunocompromised and should be placed in a private room.
82-year-old male with pneumonia/candidiasis of the groin and a 76-year-old male with upper respiratory infection/thrush. Yes, similar age and both have respiratory infections and yeast.
46-year-old male with MRSA infection and a 50-year-old male with C.difficile  infection. No, it is not good practice to place clients with different MDRO in the same room

18-year-old female that is 1-day post op appendectomy and an 84-year-old female who is agitated and confused. No, different ages and safety risk for anyone roomed with an agitated and confused client.
